title: A close galactic pair
caption: The galaxies NGC 4302 and NGC 4298, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4298, NGC 4302 · constellation Coma Berenices · about 55 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two galaxies share this Hubble view. NGC 4298, seen almost face-on, displays its spiral arms, dotted with blue areas of young stars where star birth is still going on. Its neighbour NGC 4302, seen edge-on, has a disc mottled brown by vast swathes of dust, with a burst of blue on its left side marking a region of very vigorous star formation. Both lie 55 million light-years away.
The pair were observed to celebrate Hubble's 27th year in orbit. The result is a mosaic of four separate Hubble captures stitched together to cover this wide field.

Visible and near-infrared light from the galaxies was combined to produce the colours, all captured by Wide Field Camera 3. The face-on view of NGC 4298 lays out its spiral arms, while in the edge-on NGC 4302 the dust in the disc dominates.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (4.91 x 5.25 arcminutes) and distance (55 million light years), the frame spans roughly 79,000 × 84,000 light-years. Its light set out about 55 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 combined visible and near-infrared light. The colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared component is invisible to the eye.
